scope: Targeted English review only; propagated translations are not independently attorney-approved. Original reviewer decisions are preserved, not promoted to completed signoff.

reviewerNotes.L03.q0.notes:
Generally good,  guidance is high level and includes caveats rather than absolutes. Going through each to spot any issues:
ID requests - Good,
Frisk Scope - Good
Vehicle Search - Good, but should emphasize the lower standard and the automobile exception. We call out probable cause already. 
Home Search - Good
Warrant Inspection - qualify this by saying that you "typically" or "usually" have an officer produce a search warrant if you request it, though there are cases where the warrant is sealed/classified or if it is a no knock warrant. 
Stepping Outside - I would update this to say you can speak through the door, but if you choose to step outside, do so calmly and close the door behind you. 
Biometrics - Update this to emphasize that biometrics (requiring affirmative actions) also can implicate the fifth amendment as they can be testimonial actions. Circuits are split on this currently. On passcodes, there is still some split but courts are more likely to conclude passcodes are testimonial and thus protected by the 5th amendment, though the "forgone conclusion" doctrine may still allow admissible evidence based on a forced entry of a passcode. 
Strip Searches - our statement that strip searches require a warrant is wrong. Strip searches are governed by the fourth amendment reasonableness standard. They do not always require a warrant - circuits are split on this - 3rd cir says they are required (https://www2.ca3.uscourts.gov/opinarch/252860p.pdf) but others say individualized reasonable suspicion is sufficient -
reviewerNotes.L03.q2.notes:
Right to call(s) - varies, and is based on statute. The core right is the right to contact an attorney, though the method does not have to be a call. Some states explicitly allow multiple calls, some say a "reasonable" number of calls, some say 1, some don't say anything. So the guidance should be updated to consistently reflect this "it depends" reality, yet all defendants are allowed a reasonable mechanism (typically understood to be a call) to contract their attorney
Attorney Calls Privileged - the actual rule is that the content of these calls is not admissible. It does not mean authorities can't record them and/or listen to them. Those are two different things, and thus people should still be careful what they say on calls with attorneys. 
Bail entitlement guidance - accurate, we provide general ranges and what "most" jurisdictions will do with appropriate qualifiers
Discovery duties - we don't say much about it at all on the first 24 hours page, and what we say is fine. 
Plea Instructions - the within 48-72 hours is not quite correct. A few states require 24 hours, most are in the 48-72 range. So more accurate to say ""24–72 hours depending on the state and custody status". Note that many jurisdiction also recognize "not guilty by reason of insanity" as a separate plea option.
reviewerNotes.L03.q0.authority: Riley v. California, 573 U.S. 373 (2014); Georgia v. Randolph, 547 U.S. 103 (2006); California v. Acevedo, 500 U.S. 565 (1991); United States v. Brown, 125 F.4th 1186; United States v. Payne, 99 F.4th 495; https://www.nacdl.org/Content/Compelled-Decryption-Primer;  https://www2.ca3.uscourts.gov/opinarch/252860p.pdf; Shuttlesworth v. City of Birmingham, 441 F.2d 592 (11th Cir. 1971); Flanagan v. City of North Port, 401 F.3d 1220 (11th Cir. 2005); Savino v. City of New York, 88 F.3d 74 (2d Cir. 1996); Watt v. City of Richardson, 849 F.2d 195 (5th Cir. 1988)
reviewerNotes.L03.q1.notes: Juvenille requirements - our first bullet about parental notification should be changed since it is not universally required. Rather, we should say: "Some states require police to notify a parent or guardian once a juvenile is taken into custody, but this is not required everywhere. If you are a minor, ask for your parent immediately. You have the right to do so regardless of state law, and having a parent present can help protect you during questioning.
reviewerNotes.L03.scope: See notes above. I reviewed in English and focused on the items called out above. This is not a complete content overhaul, it is a targeted review of the items called out.
reviewerNotes.L04.q0.notes:
Bail Type - We should add unsecured bonds as a common bond type. Unsecured bond (signature bond): The defendant signs an agreement promising to pay a set amount only if they fail to appear. No money is paid upfront. This is distinct from ROR — ROR has no monetary figure attached, while an unsecured bond does. It's a common middle ground courts use when they want a financial incentive without requiring cash upfront.
Missing Court - we currently say that "A warrant will be issued" if you miss court, but it's not quite that automatic. We should instead say "A warrant will almost certainly be issues" if you miss court.
reviewerNotes.L04.q2.authority: Padilla v. Kentucky; Santobello v. New York (1971)

changes.before: Right to a Phone Call
changes.after: Contacting an Attorney

changes.before: Contact family, attorney, or bail bondsman after arrest
changes.after: Access to counsel; phone rules vary by state and facility

changes.before: After being arrested and booked, you have the right to make a reasonable number of phone calls to contact an attorney, family member, or bail bondsman. Police cannot listen to calls with your attorney due to attorney-client privilege, but they may monitor other calls. It's important to use this right wisely - contact your lawyer first if possible, and avoid discussing details of your case on any call that might be recorded.
changes.after: Phone access, timing, and the number of calls vary by state and facility. Access to an attorney is protected, but it does not always take the form of a phone call. Ask staff how to contact your lawyer and arrange a confidential legal call. Ordinary jail calls may be recorded or monitored and used as evidence. Confidential attorney communications may be privileged, but calling a lawyer does not by itself make a line private. Ask your lawyer and the facility how to use the designated confidential channel before discussing the case.

changes.before: The law requires that you be formally told about the criminal charges against you, usually at your first court appearance within 48-72 hours of arrest. You have the right to know exactly what crimes you're accused of, which laws they say you broke, and what punishments you could face. This information lets you and your lawyer prepare your defense and makes sure you can't be tried for crimes you weren't properly told about.
changes.after: You have the right to be informed of the charges against you. An initial appearance often occurs within 24–72 hours, depending on the state and custody status; arraignment may occur later. This is not a universal deadline. Court paperwork and your attorney can confirm the schedule and applicable rules.

Asking for a parent is not the same as asking for a lawyer.

changes.before: Derecho a una Llamada Telefónica
changes.after: Contacto con un abogado

changes.before: Contactar a familia, abogado o fianza después del arresto
changes.after: Acceso a un abogado; las reglas telefónicas varían según el estado y el centro

changes.before: Después de ser arrestado y procesado, tiene derecho a hacer un número razonable de llamadas telefónicas para contactar a un abogado, familiar o agente de fianzas. La policía no puede escuchar llamadas con su abogado debido al privilegio abogado-cliente, pero pueden monitorear otras llamadas. Es importante usar este derecho sabiamente - contacte a su abogado primero si es posible, y evite discutir detalles de su caso en cualquier llamada que pueda ser grabada.
changes.after: El acceso al teléfono, los horarios y el número de llamadas varían según el estado y el centro. El acceso a un abogado está protegido, pero no siempre se realiza por teléfono. Pregunte al personal cómo contactar a su abogado y organizar una llamada legal confidencial. Las llamadas ordinarias desde la cárcel pueden grabarse o supervisarse y usarse como prueba. Las comunicaciones confidenciales con un abogado pueden estar protegidas por el secreto profesional, pero llamar a un abogado no convierte por sí solo una línea en privada. Pregunte a su abogado y al centro cómo usar el canal confidencial designado antes de hablar del caso.

changes.before: La Sexta Enmienda requiere que sea informado formalmente de los cargos criminales en su contra, típicamente en su lectura de cargos o comparecencia inicial dentro de 48-72 horas del arresto. Tiene derecho a saber exactamente de qué crímenes se le acusa, las leyes específicas que supuestamente violó, y las penas potenciales que enfrenta. Esta información le permite a usted y a su abogado preparar una estrategia de defensa apropiada y asegura que no pueda ser juzgado por crímenes de los que no fue debidamente notificado.
changes.after: Tiene derecho a conocer los cargos en su contra. La primera comparecencia suele ocurrir entre 24 y 72 horas, según el estado y si está bajo custodia; la lectura de cargos puede ocurrir después. No es un plazo universal. Los documentos del tribunal y su abogado pueden confirmar el calendario y las reglas aplicables.

changes.before: Derecho a una llamada telefónica
changes.after: El acceso al teléfono, los horarios y el número de llamadas varían según el estado y el centro. El acceso a un abogado está protegido, pero no siempre se realiza por teléfono. Pregunte al personal cómo contactar a su abogado y organizar una llamada legal confidencial.

changes.before: 被捕后可以联系家人、律师或保释担保人
changes.after: 获得律师帮助；通话规定因州和拘押设施而异

changes.before: 在被逮捕和登记后，你有权打合理数量的电话联系律师、家人或保释担保人。由于律师-客户特权，警察不能监听你与律师的通话，但他们可能会监听其他通话。明智地使用这项权利很重要——如果可能的话，先联系你的律师，并避免在可能被录音的电话中讨论你案件的细节。
changes.after: 能否打电话、通话时间和次数因州和拘押设施而异。联系律师受到法律保护，但不一定通过电话进行。可询问工作人员如何联系律师并安排保密的法律通话。 普通监所电话可能被录音或监听，并被用作证据。与律师的保密沟通可能受到律师与当事人保密特权的保护，但拨打律师电话本身并不意味着线路保密。讨论案情前，可向律师和拘押设施确认如何使用指定的保密渠道。

changes.before: 法律要求你被正式告知对你的刑事指控，通常是在被捕后48-72小时内的第一次出庭时。你有权知道你被指控的具体罪行、他们说你违反了哪些法律，以及你可能面临的处罚。这些信息让你和你的律师能够准备辩护，并确保你不会因为未被正式告知的罪行而受审。
changes.after: 您有权获知对您的指控。首次出庭通常在24至72小时内进行，取决于州和羁押状态；提审可能在之后进行。这并非全国统一期限。法院文书和律师可以帮助确认时间安排及适用规则。

changes.before: Police need a good reason or your permission to search
changes.after: Vehicles have fewer warrant protections than homes. Under the automobile exception, probable cause to believe a vehicle contains evidence or contraband can permit a search without a warrant or consent. This does not lower the probable-cause standard.

changes.before: If arrested, your car can be searched without permission
changes.after: Arrest alone does not authorize every vehicle search. A search incident to arrest is limited to situations where you can reach the passenger compartment or officers reasonably believe it contains evidence of the offense of arrest. Other exceptions may apply.

changes.before: You have the right to see the warrant before letting them in
changes.after: You can ask to see the warrant, and officers typically provide a copy. They are not always required to show it before entry or the search. Supporting papers may be sealed, and lawful no-knock entry can occur.

changes.before: Step outside and close door behind you to speak with officers
changes.after: You can speak through the closed door. If you choose to step outside, do so calmly and close the door behind you. This does not prevent entry when officers have lawful authority.

changes.before: Don't let officers in without seeing a warrant
changes.after: Do not physically block entry or a search because officers have not yet shown you a warrant

changes.before: Strip searches require a warrant or serious emergency
changes.after: Strip searches must satisfy the Fourth Amendment reasonableness standard; a warrant is not always required. Rules depend on the jurisdiction and setting. In the Third Circuit, strip searches incident to arrest outside jails or prisons generally require a warrant or exigent circumstances supported by probable cause. Other courts apply different standards.

changes.before: You can refuse to unlock your phone
changes.after: You can decline to consent to unlocking your phone. Whether you can be compelled to unlock it depends on the law and circumstances; a lawyer can assess any warrant or order.

changes.before: Courts are divided on biometrics: many have held police cannot force fingerprint/Face ID unlock without a warrant, but this is unsettled law that varies by jurisdiction
changes.after: Compelled fingerprint or facial unlocking can implicate the Fifth Amendment when the act communicates knowledge of or control over the device. Courts are split on when this is testimonial; having a search warrant does not by itself resolve that question.

changes.before: Passcodes are more protected — courts generally hold you cannot be compelled to reveal a passcode (5th Amendment)
changes.after: Disclosing a memorized passcode is more likely to be treated as testimonial. Courts disagree about compelled unlocking and the foregone-conclusion doctrine, which may allow compulsion when the government already knows the facts the act would communicate. Protection is not absolute.

changes.before: Don't unlock your phone for police
changes.after: A warrant to search a phone and authority to compel you to unlock it are separate legal questions

changes.before: Don't provide your passcode
changes.after: A lawyer can explain the consequences of disclosing a passcode or responding to a court order

changes.before: Don't let them use your biometrics to unlock
changes.after: Do not physically resist an attempted biometric unlock; tell your attorney what occurred

changes.before: Courts look more closely at whether a young person was truly free to leave. Many states require police to notify parents before questioning someone under 18. A minor's age is an important factor in deciding whether they felt free to go. In most states, juvenile courts give heightened scrutiny to statements made without a parent or attorney present. Minors can invoke by clearly asking for both a parent and a lawyer before answering questions.
changes.after: A minor's age matters when courts assess custody and whether a waiver was voluntary. Some states require parental notification or consultation with an attorney, but the rules differ. You can ask for a parent or guardian immediately; whether police must wait for them depends on the law and circumstances. Asking for a parent does not necessarily invoke the right to counsel. A clear request such as 'I want a lawyer' addresses that separate right.

changes.after: 《加利福尼亚州刑法》第851.5条规定，被捕者在完成登记后应立即获准完成至少三次通话，且除非客观上无法做到，最迟不得超过被捕后三小时。其他州和拘留设施的规则不同。请询问工作人员如何与律师保密联系。

changes.before: 常见答辩包括认罪和不认罪；部分法院允许不抗辩。一些司法管辖区还将因精神障碍而不负刑事责任的不认罪答辩列为单独选项，并有特殊要求。可用选项及其后果取决于当地法律和案件。律师可以在您答辩前解释这些选项。
changes.after: 答辩选项因地而异。作出答辩前，可请律师解释各项选择。
